_meta.purpose: Composable coverage cells. Each cell is a beat-sequence pattern for ONE shot (one H3 clip). Two jobs: (1) supply camera/duration deterministically so the LLM never chooses them, (2) carry prose exemplars that set the register for action / performance / reveals text.
how_to_use: Selection key is shot.function, emitted by the shots stage. One cell per shot.
Camera fields are AUTHORITATIVE — copy them into the beat row, do not ask the model for them.
duration_s values are the base rhythm. Scale the whole cell by a single factor to fit the shot's budget; NEVER rescale beats independently — the contrast between a 1.2s and a 4.0s beat is the pacing.

*_exemplar fields are few-shot material. Inject them into the beats prompt as a worked example, then ask the model to fill the same slots for THIS shot's content. Do not ship exemplar text to the video compiler.
{A}, {B}, {OBJ} are role placeholders bound to roster names at injection time.
screen_side is per-role and fixed for the duration of the cell. gaze values follow from it. If a cell is used twice in one scene, keep the same role→side binding both times.
_meta.enum_caveat: Values below use the vocabulary from scene-to-storyboard-prompt-chain.md. Map them to the actual constants in storyboard_story.py before loading — a mismatch will be silently coerced to null by the beats validator.

new_fields_assumed.kind: action | reaction | establishing | insert — beat classification. reaction beats are EXEMPT from the non-empty reveals lint.
new_fields_assumed.subjects[].performance: per-subject description of a CHANGE in the body. Not a state.
new_fields_assumed.subjects[].gaze: LOOK_L | LOOK_R | TO_CAMERA | DOWN | UP | OFF_L | OFF_R | CLOSED

_meta.register_rule: Every action and performance string names a body part and a change to it. 'She looks upset' is a state and renders as a still frame. 'The smile goes out of her face' is a change and renders as motion. This is the single property that separates the exemplars below from the output you are currently getting.

cells.notes: Neutral back-and-forth, no power shift. The load-bearing move is beat 3: cut to the LISTENER before the line finishes landing, so the audience watches the reaction rather than the delivery. Most amateur dialogue coverage cuts on the line boundary instead, and that is the single most common reason a talking scene feels flat.

subjects.performance_exemplar: sets both hands flat on the table; the chin drops a fraction before the words come
weight settled on one hip, thumb working the seam of a sleeve

beats.action_exemplar: {A} puts both hands on the table and says the first thing.
beats.reveals_exemplar: the distance between them, and who is standing closer to the door
beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: one of them has rehearsed this and the other has not
beats.sound_exemplar: a refrigerator cycling on somewhere behind them

shoulder and ear only, held still in the near foreground

subjects.performance_exemplar: the readiness goes out of the face before any reply forms; the hands come off the table
shoulder only, unmoving, in the near foreground

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the answer landed somewhere {A} had not defended

subjects.performance_exemplar: eyes drop to the tabletop and stay there; a breath goes out through the nose

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the retreat is decided before it is spoken

cells.notes: Escalation with a power shift. Two mechanisms do the work: shot size tightens monotonically, and camera height inverts between the two singles (LOW on the one gaining power, HIGH on the one losing it). Beat 5 is the tightest frame in the cell — if this shot carries is_turn, the turn lands here and nowhere else.

subjects.performance_exemplar: crosses half the distance in flat deliberate steps and stops; hands open at the sides
does not move; weight settles back onto the heels

beats.action_exemplar: {A} crosses half the distance and stops.

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the geometry of the room is already the argument
beats.sound_exemplar: footfall on bare boards, then nothing

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the quiet is the threat

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the position {B} was defending was never defensible
beats.sound_exemplar: the room's own quiet, suddenly audible

cells.notes: Look → object → reaction → new geography. The order is not decorative: the audience must see the character look BEFORE seeing the thing, or the reveal belongs to the camera instead of to the character. Beat 3 is the payload; it is a reaction beat and produces no new information by design.

subjects.performance_exemplar: the hand halts halfway to the shelf; the head turns before the body does

beats.action_exemplar: {A} stops mid-motion and looks off toward the far side of the room.

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the body registers it before {A} does
beats.sound_exemplar: a small sound, off-screen, not repeated

subjects.performance_exemplar: the eyes widen fractionally and then narrow; the breath stops; the color goes out of the mouth

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: {A} understands something that cannot now be un-understood

camera.movement_motivation: the room is bigger than it was a moment ago; the camera gives it back the space {A} has lost

subjects.performance_exemplar: does not move; stands small against the far wall with both arms at the sides
in frame with {A}, and no longer separable from the room

cells.notes: Scene opener that does NOT waste time on an empty plate. The establishing shot contains the subject already moving through it — geography and momentum in the same beat. Use this to fix 'takes too long to get to the action': the first frame of a scene should already be mid-event.
cells.applies_when: scene-opening shot, 1 subject enters or traverses a new space

subjects.performance_exemplar: already at a walk and already halfway across; the stride does not break for the doorway

beats.action_exemplar: {A} comes into the space at a walk, well past the entrance.
beats.reveals_exemplar: the whole geography, and that {A} has been moving for a while
beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: {A} came here on purpose
beats.sound_exemplar: footsteps carrying in a room with hard surfaces

camera.movement_motivation: the camera keeps pace with {A} rather than watching {A} pass

subjects.performance_exemplar: the head turns to take in the room without the feet slowing; one hand trails the wall

beats.reveals_exemplar: what {A} passes and chooses not to look at

subjects.performance_exemplar: framed by the doorway {A} is looking through, indifferent to being seen

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the scene's problem, delivered without a line of dialogue

cells.notes: Deliberately low-information. Nobody acts, nothing is revealed, someone absorbs what just happened. This cell CANNOT pass a non-empty-reveals lint and must be exempted — it is the shape your current rule set is structurally unable to produce, and its absence is why scenes read as event-event-event with no weight. Place it immediately after the turn, or after any beat carrying subtext. Note the duration contrast: 2.5 / 1.2 / 4.0. Do not smooth it.
cells.applies_when: immediately follows a high-charge beat; 1 subject

subjects.performance_exemplar: the eyes stay open a beat too long; the breath is shallow and high in the chest; nothing else moves

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the cost is being paid now, silently

subjects.performance_exemplar: the hand finds the edge of the table and stays there; the tendons stand up across the back of it

beats.action_exemplar: The hand finds the table edge and holds it.
beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the feeling goes into the object because it cannot go into the face

camera.movement_motivation: the camera retreats as the tension leaves {A}; the room comes back into the frame

subjects.performance_exemplar: sits down where {A} was standing; the shoulders come down and stay down

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the body gives up before the person decides to
beats.sound_exemplar: fabric, and a chair taking weight

cells.notes: Fast, short beats. Intent → mechanism → act → consequence → aftermath. The inserts at beats 2 and 4 are what make the action legible; without them a video model renders one continuous mushy movement. The aftermath beat is the longest in the cell and is where the scene's meaning actually sits — cutting away before it is the most common way an action moment lands as nothing.
cells.applies_when: 1 subject performs a decisive physical act

subjects.performance_exemplar: the weight shifts onto the front foot; the shoulders load; the breath goes in and stops

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the decision is made in the body first

subjects.performance_exemplar: fingers close around the handle one at a time and then all at once

beats.reveals_exemplar: the mechanism of what is about to happen
beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: commitment, at the smallest possible scale

camera.movement_motivation: the camera is destabilized by the same force {A} is applying

beats.emotional_intent_exemplar: the world answering the act
